title: After the Feigned Death
next_chapter_hook: The moment Chen Ji gently placed that chess piece, a faint pulse echoed from the depths of the Tianji Record—as if something was gazing at him through those tattered pages.

text.content: Dawn light seeped through, and in the side courtyard of the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor's residence, Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back before the window. The name card of his new identity rested on the desk—a distant cousin of the Gu family from Suzhou, called Gu Yan, an itinerant cultivator who wandered the world. He gazed down at the inked characters, a faint curve forming at the corner of his lips. Dead men had their benefits—no need to endure those pretentious pleasantries. Beyond the courtyard walls, servants swept, and he listened carefully, confirming no prying eyes before slowly exhaling a breath of turbid air. The feigned death drama had been performed for three months, and now the stage was set.

In the wooden case open on the table, neatly arranged were dozens of transmission jade talismans, three protective jade pendants, and a stack of border passage documents stamped with various seals. Chen Ji's slender fingers brushed across those objects, his gaze finally settling on a dark-gold token in the corner—that was the Crown Prince's residence token, seeing the token was like seeing the person. Three months ago, he had made a deal with that frail heir: he would eliminate the Crown Prince's nemesis, and the Crown Prince would restore his clean identity. Now the deal was complete, his "corpse" had been buried by Tianqing Sect with full disciple rites, while the real Chen Ji stood a thousand miles away, overlooking this new chess game.

He suddenly recalled his appearance when he first entered Tianqing Sect three years ago—back then, he couldn't even sense his spirit root, and was assigned to sweep fallen leaves on the Servants' Peak for a full two years. At that time, everyone looked at him with a理所当然轻蔑的眼神。Chen Ji closed his eyes, brushing those images from his mind, but a self-deprecating smile tugged at his lips. A废物? He raised his hand to press against his chest, where the Tianji Record lay quietly dormant. Three years, from a leaf-sweeping servant to where he stood today—what he'd relied on was never talent, but calculating deeper and thinking further than anyone else.

dialogue.content: My Lord, word from Xuanwu Sect.

text.content: A low voice came from outside the door. Chen Ji looked up and saw the secret sign left by the shadow guard贴在窗棂上——一朵用炭笔勾勒的墨兰。他起身将窗子推开一条缝，接过那卷细小如指的竹筒。展开，是夜清的字迹，娟秀中藏着锋锐："背叛者已伏诛，然其背后似有更高棋手操控，事涉上古禁地，详情面议。"Chen Ji将竹简凑近烛火，看着那些字迹在火光中渐渐卷曲、燃尽，眸色深沉如渊。更高棋手么……他喃喃自语，指尖在燃尽的灰烬上方虚虚一点。

dialogue.content: How interesting. Ye Qing, Ye Qing, you're getting better at keeping people in suspense.

text.content: He turned and walked back to his desk, retrieving a bronze basin from the hidden compartment and grinding the bamboo slip remnants before scattering them inside. Between the dancing flames, he remembered his first meeting with Ye Qing—when she had barged into Tianqing Sect territory as the Demonic Path Saint, bristling with killing intent, while he was nothing but a废物 who had just sensed his spirit root but couldn't even draw in spiritual energy. He had used the Tianji Record to show her a prophecy: about her future being discarded by the Holy Sect. Her expression at that time, Chen Ji remembered even now—that pair of fierce phoenix eyes filled with disbelief and overwhelming hatred.

Three years of cooperation, and Ye Qing had never asked why he could foresee the future. This tacit understanding pleased Chen Ji greatly—smart people didn't need too many explanations. He took from his breast pocket a transmission talisman carved with Ye Qing's aura, was about to activate it, but paused. Ancient Forbidden Land... these four characters carried weight beyond anyone else's understanding. The ruins opened in the first volume were merely the tip of the iceberg; the true core of the forbidden land held something even the Eyes of Heavenly Will coveted. His gaze flickered, and the Tianji Record at his chest pulsed warmly, as if responding to his thoughts.

choice.prompt: Ye Qing's intelligence report involves the Ancient Forbidden Land and a higher chess player; Chen Ji needs to decide how to respond to this new variable

choices.text: Travel personally to the Demonic Path Holy Sect for a face-to-face secret discussion with Ye Qing
choices.description: This matter carries tremendous weight and requires personally verifying the intelligence's authenticity. A personal visit, though time-consuming, demonstrates sincerity.
choices.visible_cost: Exposure risk increases, potentially delaying other arrangements
choices.visible_reward: Obtain first-hand intelligence and finalize cooperation details with Ye Qing face-to-face
choices.risk_hint: The Demonic Path territory is perilous; sufficient trump cards must be brought

text.content: Chen Ji returned the transmission talisman to his sleeve, rose, and pushed open the hidden door to the inner chamber. Behind the door was a tiny secret room, where a black cloak that could conceal aura hung on the wall, and three life-saving talismans lay quietly in a jade box in the corner. He took down the cloak and draped it over his shoulders, adjusting his features before a bronze mirror—the person in the mirror had delicate features, with an carefree air befitting an itinerant cultivator, nothing like the cowardly废物 of Tianqing Sect. Good. He pushed open the door and stepped out; morning wind brushed his face, carrying the distinctive crispness of early autumn. Three months—it was time to get some fresh air.

choices.text: Send a reply to Ye Qing, meeting at the tri-border in three days
choices.description: Maintain an air of mystery, letting Ye Qing reveal more on her own. Personally braving danger isn't the best strategy; distant manipulation better maintains initiative.
choices.visible_cost: Might miss crucial details, Ye Qing may think sincerity lacking
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the advantage of mystery, avoid exposing movements prematurely
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing may hold back; intelligence completeness questionable

text.content: Chen Ji put the transmission talisman away again, fingers gently tapping its surface, carving a cipher only Ye Qing could understand: "Three days hence, at Qingyun Ferry. If you don't come, I'll assume you've been recruited by that 'higher chess player.'" At the signature, he hesitated briefly, finally adding an odd symbol—their secret sign meaning "this matter has traps, verify carefully." He sealed the talisman in a bamboo tube and tossed it out the window. A moment later, a shadow streaked across the sky; the tube vanished. Chen Ji stood beneath the eaves, watching the fading silhouette, eyes flashing with sharp light.

choices.text: Use the Tianji Record to foresee this matter; results within three hours
choices.description: Exchange Heavenly Fate Value for prophecy, confirming Ye Qing's intelligence credibility and who that "higher chess player" truly is.
choices.visible_cost: Consumes 5 points of Heavenly Fate; Chen Ji's destiny was already running thin
choices.visible_reward: Foresee the truth in advance, avoid being deceived by anyone
choices.risk_hint: Each use of the Tianji Record brings backlash; the more complete the fragment, the heavier the backlash

text.content: Chen Ji reflected quietly, then finally placed his palm over his chest. The fragment grew warm in his palm, and a familiar force spread from his fingertips. He closed his eyes, letting that force drag him into the current of fate—three breaths later, he saw. At Qingyun Ferry three days hence, Ye Qing would go alone, yet encounter an ambush midway. The ambusher was no other than her most trusted protector. The larger problem: behind that protector stood Ling Yuan's shadow. And behind Ling Yuan... the image suddenly blurred, as if some force was deliberately obscuring it. Chen Ji opened his eyes abruptly, fine cold sweat already beading on his forehead.

choices.memory_label: 窥见夜清被伏击的预言

text.content: Ling Yuan. That name was like a thorn, embedded deep in Chen Ji's heart. The old Sect Master of Tianqing Sect, seemingly his benefactor who elevated him from Servants' Peak, yet secretly repeatedly setting traps. Chen Ji still remembered Ling Yuan's gaze the first time he saw him—not looking at a废物, but at an eyesore blocking the path. Even then, he had wondered: what was this old fox afraid of? Now the answer was clear: the Tianji Record's inheritance had always belonged to the capable. Ling Yuan had lost to Chen Xuan back then; now he wanted to repeat the trick, to put Chen Ji to death.

Chen Ji walked to the bookshelf, pulling from the very bottom a dusty journal. It was intelligence he'd collected over three years regarding Ling Yuan, the Eyes of Heavenly Will, and the legendary Ancient Forbidden Land. On the journal's last page was recorded something Mo Xiansheng had once told him: "The Tianji Record is not the strongest prophetic artifact; it's merely one of the pieces Heaven's Will has placed in the mortal world. Every generation's inheritor was favored by destiny—and every one was abandoned by it." He stared at those words for a long while, then suddenly laughed softly. Pieces? He would make himself the chess player.

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng, what other secrets are hidden in that first page?

text.content: He closed the journal, fingertips caressing the worn characters on the cover. Three years, from废物 to chess player—every step he'd taken was on a blade's edge. Han Lie's provocations, Su Qingyao's probings, Ling Yuan's veiled attacks... how many wanted to see him dead, yet he insisted on surviving, not just surviving but watching them one by one fall into the abyss. Now, the feigned death was complete, the final showdown imminent. He stood at fate's crossroads; behind him were three years of endurance and scheming, before him lay unknown dangers and the Tianji Record fragment's backlash. Chen Ji took a deep breath, then slowly exhaled.

choice.prompt: Facing the approaching final showdown, Chen Ji needs to clarify his strategic stance

choices.text: Steady defense and patience; respond to changes without changing
choices.description: Continue hiding in the shadows, letting various forces exhaust each other; strike to kill when the moment ripens.
choices.visible_cost: Might miss the first-mover advantage, allowing enemies to set up first
choices.visible_reward: Maximize self-preservation, maintain information differential advantage
choices.risk_hint: The Eyes of Heavenly Will and Ling Yuan won't give him much time

text.content: Chen Ji turned back to his desk, took up a brush, and wrote a single character on xuan paper: "Still." The strokes were bold, and before the ink had dried, he crumpled the paper and threw it into the bronze basin. Still waters run deep; beneath the depths lie hidden reefs—this was his style. He placed the Crown Prince's token into the hidden compartment, then hung the black cloak back on the wall. Having completed all this, he leaned back in his chair, eyes closed, resting. Since the final showdown was unavoidable, let it come later still; let his enemies' arrogance bury them.

choices.text: Take the initiative to strike, prematurely triggering contradictions among various forces
choices.description: Utilizing the chaos from the feigned death, publicly expose Ling Yuan, Han Lie, and others' schemes, triggering internal strife among them.
choices.visible_cost: Exposure risk surges; potentially making too many enemies simultaneously
choices.visible_reward: Profit from chaos; one stone stirs a thousand waves
choices.risk_hint: Requires precise control of rhythm, otherwise the fire may burn oneself

text.content: Chen Ji opened his eyes, cold light flashing in his gaze. He retrieved several blank jade talismans from the hidden compartment, and with flowing spiritual energy at his fingertips, began carving one by one—those were contents of forged secret letters, "evidence" of Ling Yuan colluding with the Demonic Path, Han Lie secretly hoarding forbidden arts, Han Lie and Ling Yuan secretly conspiring. A cold smile tugged at his lips. Fake? Irrelevant. What mattered was, when these "evidence" simultaneously appeared before the three great sects, no one would have time to pursue the truth. A flurry of fists kills the master—his favorite tactic.

choices.text: Contact Su Qingyao, bringing her into the core scheme
choices.description: Su Qingyao is the only one who sensed the truth; rather than continuing opposition, turn enemy into ally, making her a piece in the open.
choices.visible_cost: Su Qingyao has a fierce personality; may not be trusted, and could expose movements
choices.visible_reward: Gain a powerful insider who can maintain secret contact with Tianqing Sect
choices.risk_hint: If Su Qingyao反向利用情报，后果不堪设想

text.content: Chen Ji paused his hand, gaze falling on a dusty jade box in the corner. Inside were three transmission talismans he had personally refined, capable of penetrating any barrier to directly contact Su Qingyao. He had circled this Inner Sect Senior Fellow for two full years; she had come infinitely close to the truth three times, and three times he had design化解。如今假死已成定局，继续瞒下去已无意义。He sighed softly, taking out the jade box. To end all this, he needed an insider—and Su Qingyao was the most suitable candidate.

The sun climbed higher, and the shadows in the courtyard shifted half an inch. Chen Ji stood before the window, watching those mottled lights dance on the ground, and suddenly remembered his days on Servants' Peak. Back then he had to rise before dawn every day to sweep, not resting until sunset. Sometimes when exhausted, he would lean against an old locust tree, gazing blankly at sunlight filtering through leaves. That version of him had never imagined standing at such a height one day, overlooking the entire board of clouds and wind. He reached up to tidy his hair; the bronze mirror reflected a calm face—unruffled, deep as the abyss.

dialogue.content: A废物? Then let this废物 personally bury you all.

text.content: The words had barely fallen when the Tianji Record at his chest suddenly quivered. It wasn't the burning sensation of using prophecy, but an extremely faint pulse—as if something was awakening from slumber, or as if a gaze was透过那薄薄的纸页，正注视着他。Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, hand instinctively pressing his chest. The fragment lay still in his palm, yet that indescribable sense of being watched persisted. He closed his eyes, trying to probe with his spiritual sense, only to touch emptiness. Higher existence... he murmured, a flash of indescribable coldness crossing his gaze. The Eyes of Heavenly Will? Or something else?

He stood motionless for a long while. The sunlight beyond the window remained bright, servants in the courtyard continued coming and going; everything appeared no different from the usual. But Chen Ji knew: from this moment, something had quietly changed. He slowly released the hand pressed to his chest, lowering his gaze to the fragment hidden beneath his collar. Tianji Record, a piece placed by Heaven... could the chess player also be watching him from upon this board? Chen Ji drew a deep breath, pressing that fleeting tremor into his heart's depths. Regardless—this game, he must win.

He walked back to his desk, collecting the scattered jade talismans one by one. Having finished, he suddenly reached up and took the ink-filled wolf-hair brush from the desk. Xuan paper spread out; after a moment's contemplation, the brush fell, writing four characters: "The chess exists before the game." The ink glistened, like some silent declaration. Chen Ji gazed at those four characters, his lips slowly curving. This grand drama spanning three years was finally approaching its most brilliant climax. And he, Chen Ji—this废物 once trampled beneath everyone's feet—would personally grasp this hand that places the pieces, stirring the winds and clouds across the heavens.

Morning bells rang, and the long street outside the mansion gradually grew lively. Chen Ji rolled up that calligraphy and stored it in the hidden compartment, then turned to push open his door. Early autumn wind rushed to meet him, carrying a chill. He stood with hands clasped behind his back on the veranda, gazing toward Tianqing Sect in the distance, his gaze deep and dark as ink. Three months of feigned death—it was time to close the net. Ye
